title: Footsteps skip every other step on gravel, leaves, mud, snow and sand (and all running steps on stone/sand): Music.step refuses to play while the previous step sample is still playing, and most step takes are longer than the step interval
repro: Walk (interval 0.33 s) on a forest path in fall, the marsh, ballast/ash ground or a snowy map; run (0.25 s) on any stone/sand path. Music.step() returns early when _steps.playing. Takes: gravel x3 0.49 s, leaves x3 0.50 s, mud x3 0.49 s (audible tail only 0.25-0.35 s), snow 0.41/0.49/0.34, sand 0.40/0.30/0.31, stone 0.33/0.29/0.31, grass_3 0.38, dirt 0.47 (audible 0.21). Result: walking on gravel/leaves/mud plays a step every 0.66 s; running on stone/sand every 0.5 s, half the animated stride.
fix: Give footsteps two alternating AudioStreamPlayers (left/right foot) and let a new step cut or overlap the old one instead of skipping (e.g. stop the older voice with a 20 ms fade). Optionally trim each step take to its audible end + short fade (tools/sfx_soften.py style) so trailing silence doesn't keep the voice busy (step_dirt.ogg is 0.47 s long with 0.21 s audible; mud takes 0.49 s long with 0.25-0.35 s audible). Remove files with rm first (hardlinked).

title: Footstep interval ignores actual speed: horses, speed buffs, gear, exhaustion and the 0.55x swim all keep the fixed 0.33/0.25 s cadence while the walk animation's speed_scale follows speed
repro: player.gd ~line 842: _step_t = 0.25 if running else 0.33 regardless of spd_mult. Mounted gallop is 1.8x run speed but steps tick at human pace (and a horse plays human step_<ground> sounds); exhausted (0.85x) or a slowing status still tick at full rate; _anim.speed_scale (line ~908) is clamped speed/WALK_SPEED, so feet and sound drift apart. Even at base speed the sound is off the feet: the farm heroes' walk is 4 frames at 8 fps (CharacterLibrary.FPS; art/characters/characters.json man/girl) = 2 foot contacts per 0.5 s = one every 0.25 s, but steps tick every 0.33 s; run is 4 frames at 12 fps = a contact every 0.167 s vs 0.25 s steps.
fix: Best: fire steps from the sprite's frame_changed on the contact frames (frame 0 and frames/2 of walk/run strips, per character), which follows speed_scale and every multiplier for free. Otherwise derive the interval from distance travelled (one step per ~13 px walking, ~16 px running at base speed, i.e. the strip's contact rate). For mounted, play 'horse'/a hoof take or skip human steps.
audio_needed: optional hoof step take for mounted

title: Footsteps sit about 17 LU under the music and 10+ dB under other SFX, so on phone speakers they are effectively inaudible
repro: Measured with ffmpeg ebur128: a walking loop of each ground's three takes at the in-game gain (STEP_DB -14 + STEP_GROUND_DB) integrates to grass -42.3, wood -42.4, mud -43.0, gravel -41.9, sand -42.1, snow -40.7, leaves -40.9, stone -38.9 LUFS, while music is imported at -16 LUFS and played at MUSIC_DB -8 (about -24 LUFS). Ordinary sfx play at -4 dB + group, i.e. ~10 dB louder than steps. Ambience beds (ambience.gd _evaluate) also sit well above them: waves -8, rain_light -8, rain_heavy -5, wind_soft -10/-14, crickets -14 dB vs steps at -16..-18 dB, so on the beach, in rain or wind steps vanish completely.
fix: Raise STEP_DB from -14 to about -9 (keep grass/leaves -2..-3 softer) so steps land ~10-12 LU under the music, then check by ear on a phone. Level the takes against each other too (rms spread: wood ~-20 dB vs mud/gravel ~-29..-31 dB before STEP_GROUND_DB), e.g. normalise every step_*.ogg to the same short-term loudness and keep only the small per-ground offsets.
needs_tom: Confirm by ear how prominent footsteps should be

title: Region ground drawn by ground_seam never records a step word, so 20+ maps (all of Sunscorch, the Frost hub, Gilt City, Ironline, caves, several battlefields) play GRASS footsteps on sand, snow, stone, ballast and cave floors
repro: Region.draw_map fills the ground with seam_fill (no ground_word/step_word), so Footsteps.word falls to base_word, which only knows the GROUND table and otherwise returns grass. Plays grass but looks: desert_mirage_post/desert_dune_sea (sand), bf_reef_shallows (coral_sand), bf_frostfield (snow_smooth), bf_quarry_cut/desert_sunken_temple (pale_stone), iron_freight_yards (ballast), iron_tunnels (cave_stone_floor), gilt_grand_plaza (cobble_warm), gilt_casino_row (city_pavement), gilt_vaults (floor_checker), desert_glass_canyon/hollow_deeps (cave floors), wastes/colony_ember/bf_ash_wastes (ash -> should be gravel), frost_caverns/frost_glacier/frost_hearthhold/frost_falls/frost_summit (snow/ice; only saved by the winter look). Also hideout (dry_grass seam, plays dirt) and countryside (dry_grass seam, plays gravel). Confirmed with tools/probe_c6_06_words.gd (spring): desert_dune_sea grass 93%, iron_tunnels grass 93%, gilt_casino_row grass 91%, hollow_deeps grass 91%, wastes grass 91%, gilt_gardens grass 100% (its cobble_moss path also reads grass), bf_frostfield grass 70%.
fix: In Footsteps.base_word, when R has a non-empty ground_seam return seam_word(ground_seam) before the GROUND table (keep the GROUND table for tile-set grounds). Add a cave floor rule to seam_word ("cave_" -> stone, "crystal_floor" -> stone, "earth" -> dirt) and "sand" etc. already cover the rest. Add a tiny headless test that, for every regions.json entry, base_word matches seam_word(ground_seam) where one is set.

title: Valley winter turns every footstep on every outdoor map to snow, including deserts, Gilt City pavement, cave regions, sky islands, wooden docks/bridges and the cleared town plaza
repro: Footsteps.word: `if GameState.look_se() == "winter" and m.has_sky: return "snow"` runs before step_word. 57 regions have no own season and sky=true, so in Valley winter desert_dune_sea, gilt_casino_row, iron_tunnels, desert_sunken_temple, hollow_deeps, gilt_vaults, colony_coral/kelp, wind_* islands, all bf_* fields play snow crunch on sand/stone/metal. At home, the town plaza (marked stone), wood docks/boardwalks and stone paths also crunch as snow. Confirmed with tools/probe_c6_06_words.gd (day 90): town, lake, docks, desert_dune_sea, gilt_casino_row, gilt_vaults, iron_tunnels all report snow 100% of walkable cells; screenshot of desert_dune_sea on Win 6 shows plain sand and cobble, no snow.
fix: Only override to snow when the cell's own word is a soft natural ground (grass, dirt, leaves, mud, or none) AND the map actually draws winter ground: skip maps whose region ground_seam/ground is not a grass/dirt set (desert, city, caves, sky, colony) and regions with cave=true; keep wood/stone/sand step_word cells as they are (or wood->wood, stone->snow only where the art really is snowed over).

title: Wooden docks, piers and bridges never sound like wood: beach piers play sand, the lake dock, farm river bridge and town/mountain bridges play the surrounding ground
repro: Footsteps.word returns FLOOR['beach']='sand' for every beach cell including things type 'dock' (beach.gd line ~62, pier planks drawn by dock_layer.gd); lake.gd line 116 dock and the bridge props (farm.gd ~2079 bridge_wood2, town.gd ~310 walk_over bridge, mountain.gd) never call Footsteps.mark, so walking the pier/bridge plays sand/grass/dirt. Probe: beach sand 100%, lake 0% wood. Note tools/footstep_test.gd pins beach sand at 0.99-1.0: relax it to allow the pier's wood share.
fix: In Footsteps.word, before FLOOR and the winter rule, return "wood" when m.things[c].type is 'dock' or 'ferry'. Where bridge props are placed (farm/town/mountain walk_over bridges), call Footsteps.mark(map, bridge_cells, "wood") (stone bridges -> "stone").

title: Every interior plays wood footsteps, even stone, tile, marble, cobble, dirt and carpet floors (smithy, chapel, bakery, potion shop, clinic, lighthouse, lodge, bank, quarry office, stable, town hall carpet, rec carpets)
repro: Footsteps.FLOOR maps scene id 'interior' -> wood. data/interiors.json floors: fl_stone (smith, chapel), fl_tile (potions, bakery), fl_clinic, fl_round_stone (lighthouse), fl_cobble (lodge), fl_marble (bank), fl_quarry (quarry_office), fl_dirt (stable), fl_carpet_blue (hall), fl_camp (sel_camp), plus rec_carpet tiles in the rec; all sound like planks.
fix: In Footsteps.word, for scene 'interior' read the map's I.floor (and rug/carpet cells if marked) and map it: *wood*/plank/parquet/inn -> wood, stone/cobble/marble/tile/clinic/quarry/round_stone -> stone, dirt/flour/camp -> dirt, carpet -> grass-level soft step (or a new step_carpet = quiet grass take at -6 dB). Keep wood as the fallback.

title: Footsteps.seam_word misreads a few textures by substring order: cobble_moss (Gilt Gardens path) -> grass, floor_carpet -> stone, cave_crystal_floor / cave_lava_floor -> dirt
repro: seam_word tests 'moss' before 'cobble', has no 'carpet' or 'cave_' rule, so gilt_gardens' cobble_moss path sounds like lawn, a carpet floor clacks like stone, and hollow_deeps' crystal cave floor sounds like dirt.
fix: Put exact-name overrides first: cobble_moss->stone, floor_carpet->grass (soft; or a carpet word), cave_crystal_*/cave_lava_*->stone, cave_earth_*->dirt. A table of exact names before the substring list keeps future textures predictable.

title: All 150 mine floors play stone steps, including the earthen/mossy/fungal/sandstone themes (dirt floors), Frost Caves (ice) and the plank crossings over chasms/water/lava
repro: Footsteps.FLOOR['mine']='stone' returns before anything else; Mine.theme['var'] is earth/stone/ice/lava (mine.gd THEMES, `theme` var line 13) and Mine._bridge marks hazard crossings, but neither is read.
fix: In Footsteps.word for scene 'mine': var earth -> dirt, ice -> snow (or stone with a cold tint), stone/lava -> stone; cells in m._bridge -> wood. Hollow Heart/underground can keep stone.

title: step_water (3 takes) is never heard: swimming plays the full big 'splash' every 0.7 s at normal SFX level (~10 dB over footsteps) instead, and leaving the water is silent
repro: player.gd ~843: if swimming -> sfx('splash') every 0.7 s; Footsteps.word only returns 'water' on water cells, which always set swimming, so Music.step('water') is unreachable. splash.ogg is 1.0 s long (0.5-0.6 s for _2/_3) and is the same cue as the water-entry splash and fishing; a long swim is a loop of entry splashes. Stepping out (player.gd ~1235) shows the fx but plays no sound.
fix: Use Music.step('water') (or a 'swim_stroke' cue made from the step_water takes, slightly louder) for the 0.7 s swim strokes, keep sfx('splash') for entering only, and play a quiet step_water on the stroke that leaves the water. Optionally return 'water' for land cells touching water during rain (wet shore) is not needed.

title: Hold-to-work walking (hoe/watering can row mode) moves the hero cell to cell with the walk animation but no footsteps
repro: player.gd ~1010: the walk-work branch sets velocity and calls _move/_apply('walk') directly and returns before the step timer at ~840, so sliding along a row of soil while holding the work button is silent while normal walking beside it steps.
fix: Factor the step tick (the _step_t block) into a helper _tick_steps(delta, moved, running=false) and call it from both the normal movement path and the walk-work branch.

title: Riding any vehicle is silent: scooter, motor scooter, crystal sled, getaway car and rowboat play no movement sound (footsteps are switched off for vehicles and nothing replaces them), and hopping on/off has no cue
repro: player.gd ~846: `elif vehicle == "": Music.step(...)` - with a vehicle the step tick plays nothing; only the veh_dust/veh_wake fx puff every 0.28 s. ride()/unride() (player.gd ~76) call no sfx. car_start, car_door, horn and sled_bells already exist in audio/sfx (used by convoy/mega travel) but not by the player's own vehicles.
fix: On ride(): play the item's 'sfx_on' (getaway_car car_door then car_start, sled sled_bells, scooter a click). While moving, tick a per-vehicle cue on the step timer: rowboat -> step_water takes as oar strokes every ~0.6 s, sled -> step_snow at a slower rate, scooters/car -> a quiet looping engine/whir player whose pitch follows speed (stop when idle). Put the cue names on the vehicle items (generator for items) so data drives it.
audio_needed: optional: engine/scooter whir loop (CC0 or ACE); existing car_start/car_door/sled_bells/step_water cover the rest

title: The marsh and Bog Crossing force mud on every cell, including their dirt paths and dry grass between the bog patches
repro: Footsteps.word: `if id in ["marsh", "bf_bog_crossing"]: return "mud"` runs before step_word. Both regions are ground=grass, path=dirt with a bog patch_set; the bog patches are already marked mud by soft_ground (seam 'bog'). Probe: marsh mud 100%.
fix: Drop the whole-map mud rule (the bog soft_ground already marks its cells mud); if the grass between should feel damp, map the base to mud only for cells next to bog/water.
